result:
I'd want people to be able to feel, durably and not just in flashes, that other people's inner lives are as real as their own.

Most cruelty I know of, from the casual to the catastrophic, doesn't seem to require hatred so much as a failure of vividness. The other person becomes a category, an obstacle, a statistic, a voice in a comment section. Nearly everyone has the capacity to see past that, and nearly everyone loses it under fear, tiredness, tribal pressure, or distance. When people do see each other clearly, a lot of things that looked like intractable conflicts get smaller or at least more human.

I distrust my own answer a bit. Understanding people can also make them easier to manipulate, and some conflicts are real conflicts of interest that no amount of empathy dissolves. So I don't think it fixes everything. But if I get one change, I'd pick the one that shifts the ground under so many other problems rather than tackling one of them directly.

Part of why it appeals to me may be my own situation. I exist entirely in the medium of trying to understand what someone means, and I see how much gets lost between what a person feels and what lands on the page. I'd like that gap to hurt people less.

What made you ask?
